header:
Why Verizon gives
away free phones

lines.text: In 2025, Verizon sold devices for $3.5 billion below cost.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, Verizon sold devices three point five billion below cost.

lines.text: Its FY2025 10-K shows $25.5 billion in device revenue, $29.0 billion in costs. On purpose.
lines.say: Its annual report shows twenty-five point five billion in device revenue, twenty-nine billion in costs. On purpose.

lines.text: The real money is the bill: $83.7 billion in service revenue in 2025.
lines.say: The real money is the bill: eighty-three point seven billion in service revenue in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Free phones usually mean 36 monthly credits, often on a premium plan, and leaving ends them.
lines.say: Free phones usually mean thirty-six monthly credits, often on a premium plan, and leaving ends them.

lines.text: Example: an $830 phone credited $23.06 a month x 36 = $830.16.
lines.say: Say an eight hundred thirty dollar phone gets about twenty-three dollars a month for thirty-six months.

lines.text: If that plan costs $25 more a month, that's $900.
lines.say: If that plan costs twenty-five dollars more a month, that's nine hundred dollars.

lines.text: And customers stick: consumer phone churn stayed under 1% a month through 2025.
lines.say: And customers stick: consumer phone churn stayed under one percent a month through twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Each consumer account paid $147.36 a month on average in Q4 2025.
lines.say: Each consumer account paid about a hundred forty-seven dollars a month in late twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: The phone opens the door. The plan pays for it.
lines.say: The phone opens the door. The plan pays for it.

post.title: Why Verizon sold devices $3.5B below cost in 2025
post.ig:
In 2025, Verizon sold devices for $3.5 billion below cost.
FY2025 10-K: $25.5B wireless equipment revenue vs $29.0B cost of wireless equipment.
The money is the plan: $83.7B wireless service revenue in 2025, and consumer ARPA of $147.36 a month in Q4 2025.
Free phones are usually 36 monthly bill credits, often tied to a premium unlimited plan; leaving early ends them. Example: $23.06 x 36 = $830.16, while a $25/month pricier plan is $900 over 36 months.
Consumer phone churn stayed under 1% a month every quarter of 2024-2025.
Sources: Verizon FY2025 10-K, 4Q25 Financial and Operating Information, Droid-Life, WhistleOut.
News and education, not financial advice.
